builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Realizing Low-Precision Storage and Sparse Execution in a Folded FPGA Speech Enhancer
summary: The method replaces uniform hardware-aware compression driven by a single bit-operation metric with training objectives that separately price on-chip weight storage (mixed precision) and removable scheduled work (structured channel sparsity) for a folded streaming accelerator. It requires FPGA deployment (a Kria KV260), bit-exact hardware-software co-design, and retraining with group-lasso objectives, which is a substantial engineering cost; notably, reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits saves 27% dynamic power but under 5% latency, so precision work alone underdelivers. It can fail if the target workload's sparsity pattern does not align with the engine's schedule, if plain group-lasso degrades task quality on non-speech tasks, or if results do not transfer to GPU inference where folding economics do not apply.
rationale: The gains are real but measured on a specific folded FPGA speech-enhancement accelerator, and the reader has no FPGA, so the actionable takeaway is the principle—price storage and removable work separately—rather than direct adoption.
technique: Cost-aware mixed precision and channel sparsity for folded FPGA inference

claims.statement: The method replaces uniform hardware-aware compression driven by a single bit-operation metric with training objectives that separately price on-chip weight storage (mixed precision) and removable scheduled work (structured channel sparsity) for a folded streaming accelerator. It requires FPGA deployment (a Kria KV260), bit-exact hardware-software co-design, and retraining with group-lasso objectives, which is a substantial engineering cost; notably, reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits saves 27% dynamic power but under 5% latency, so precision work alone underdelivers. It can fail if the target workload's sparsity pattern does not align with the engine's schedule, if plain group-lasso degrades task quality on non-speech tasks, or if results do not transfer to GPU inference where folding economics do not apply.

Structured channel sparsity removes 47.3% of convolution MACs, cutting frame time by 45% (1.86 to 1.03 ms) and dynamic energy by 60% (83 to 33 uJ/frame) on a Kria KV260, with higher speech quality than the storage-priced baseline.
